summary: Treating the 8x768 shape as an unjustified prior paid off: at a fixed 300s budget the best shape I found is depth 10 x dim 640 with head_dim 128 and TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2**17, giving val_bpb 0.988531 vs the 1.012347 cell baseline (width 768->640 alone got 0.990125, adding depth got the rest). The decisive measurement was a CPU-only profile of make_dataloader: it costs ~113ms per 131072-token batch (~46ms tokenize+parquet, ~15-40ms best-fit scan, ~9ms row fill) against 110-124ms steps, so throughput is dataloader-bound and shrinking the model buys almost no extra tokens -- which is why 8x512 (1.007564) and batch 2**16 (1.010386) both lost badly. What did not work: value embeddings on every layer (0.990844, a wash), head_dim 64 with 10 heads at FLOP parity (0.997068, clearly worse), and the smaller batch. Next I would attack the dataloader itself, since roughly 50ms per step is GIL-bound Python packing that a background worker in a separate interpreter could hide, and that is likely worth more than further shape tuning; after that, push depth to 12-14 at width 640 and retune the Muon LR for the deeper stack.
